title: Imports and Namespace
content: Imports Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.Basic` for graph definitions, `SimpleGraph.Coloring` for proper colorings and the `Coloring` type, and `SimpleGraph.Subgraph` for subgraph infrastructure. The `SimpleGraph` namespace provides the `Adj` relation and `bot_adj` lemma used throughout.
mathContext: Mathlib models simple graphs as symmetric irreflexive relations on a vertex type $V$. A proper $k$-coloring is a function $c : V \to \text{Fin}(k)$ with $G.\text{Adj}\,v\,w \Rightarrow c(v) \neq c(w)$, wrapped in the `SimpleGraph.Coloring` type.

title: Problem Overview
content: **Erdős Problem #923** asks: for every $k$, is there $f(k)$ such that $\chi(G) \geq f(k)$ implies $G$ has a triangle-free subgraph with $\chi \geq k$? Answer: YES (Rödl 1977). The threshold $f(k)$ is a tower of 2s of height $\sim k$. The proof uses Ramsey-theoretic edge partition arguments.
mathContext: The problem lies at the intersection of chromatic graph theory and Ramsey theory. It asks whether chromatic complexity must 'spread' beyond triangles: even after removing all triangles, a graph with high enough $\chi$ retains a subgraph of moderately high $\chi$. The tower-type growth of $f(k)$ is intrinsic, reflecting that Ramsey numbers $R(3, t) = \Theta(t^2/\log t)$ grow polynomially, but iterated applications yield towers.

title: Chromatic Number
content: $\chi(G) = \inf\{k \in \mathbb{N} : \exists\, c : V \to \text{Fin}(k),\, c \text{ is a proper coloring}\}$. The chromatic number is the minimum number of colors needed for a proper vertex coloring. Defined via `sInf` on the set of valid color counts.
mathContext: For finite graphs, $\chi(G)$ always exists and equals $\min\{k : G \text{ is } k\text{-colorable}\}$. Key bounds include $\chi(G) \leq \Delta(G) + 1$ (greedy/Brooks), $\chi(G) \geq \omega(G)$ (clique number), and $\chi(G) \geq |V|/\alpha(G)$ (independence number). The `noncomputable` annotation reflects that computing $\chi(G)$ is NP-hard in general.

title: k-Colorability
content: `IsKColorable G k` means $\chi(G) \leq k$, i.e., $G$ admits a proper coloring with at most $k$ colors.
mathContext: The $k$-colorability predicate is monotone: if $G$ is $k$-colorable, it is also $(k+1)$-colorable. The decision problem '$G$ is $k$-colorable?' is polynomial for $k \leq 2$ (bipartiteness test) but NP-complete for $k \geq 3$.

title: High Chromatic Number
content: `HasChromaticNumberAtLeast G k` means $\chi(G) \geq k$. This is the precondition for Rödl's theorem: the graph must have chromatic number at least $f(k)$.
mathContext: High chromatic number does not imply the existence of large cliques. Mycielski (1955) and the Zykov construction produce triangle-free graphs with $\chi$ as large as desired, showing $\chi$ and $\omega$ can be arbitrarily far apart. Random graphs $G(n, p)$ typically have $\chi \sim n/(2\log_b n)$ where $b = 1/(1-p)$.

title: Triangle and Triangle-Free
content: **HasTriangle** $G$: $\exists\, a,b,c \in V$ pairwise distinct with $G.\text{Adj}\,a\,b \land G.\text{Adj}\,b\,c \land G.\text{Adj}\,a\,c$. **IsTriangleFree** $G = \neg\text{HasTriangle}\,G$. Triangle-freeness is equivalent to the graph having girth $\geq 4$.
mathContext: A triangle is a copy of $K_3$. Triangle-free graphs on $n$ vertices have at most $\lfloor n^2/4 \rfloor$ edges (Mantel's theorem, 1907), with equality for the complete bipartite graph $K_{\lfloor n/2\rfloor, \lceil n/2\rceil}$. The Ramsey number $R(3, t) = \Theta(t^2/\log t)$ (Kim 1995, Bohman-Keevash 2010) governs the independence number of triangle-free graphs.

title: emptyGraph_triangleFree
content: The empty graph $\bot$ (no edges) is triangle-free. Proved by unfolding definitions, applying `push_neg`, and using `bot_adj` (which states $\bot.\text{Adj}\,v\,w = \text{False}$). One of only two fully proved results in the file.
mathContext: The proof is purely logical: $\neg\exists\,a\,b\,c,\, \bot.\text{Adj}\,a\,b$ holds vacuously since $\bot.\text{Adj} = \lambda\,v\,w,\, \text{False}$. The tactic chain `unfold; push_neg; intros; simp [bot_adj]` demonstrates how Lean handles existential negation with the `push_neg` tactic from Mathlib.

title: Spanning and Induced Subgraphs
content: **IsSpanningSubgraph** $H\,G$: same vertex set, $E(H) \subseteq E(G)$. **inducedSubgraph** $G\,S$: the subgraph of $G$ on vertex set $S \subseteq V$, using `comap` to restrict adjacency to the subtype.
mathContext: A spanning subgraph preserves all vertices but may remove edges. For Rödl's theorem, the triangle-free subgraph $H$ is a spanning subgraph of $G$, meaning we only delete edges (those participating in triangles). The induced subgraph $G[S]$ restricts both vertices and edges: $G[S].\text{Adj}\,u\,v \iff G.\text{Adj}\,u.\text{val}\,v.\text{val}$.

title: Subgraph Chromatic Monotonicity
content: **Axiom**: $\chi(H) \leq \chi(G)$ whenever $H$ is a spanning subgraph of $G$. Any proper coloring of $G$ remains proper for $H$ since removing edges only relaxes constraints.
mathContext: If $c : V \to \{1,\ldots,k\}$ is a proper $k$-coloring of $G$, then for any $H$ with $E(H) \subseteq E(G)$, the coloring $c$ is also proper for $H$: $H.\text{Adj}\,u\,v \Rightarrow G.\text{Adj}\,u\,v \Rightarrow c(u) \neq c(v)$. Hence $\chi(H) \leq \chi(G)$.

title: Mycielski's Theorem
content: **Axiom** (Mycielski, 1955): For every $k$, there exists a triangle-free graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \geq k$. The Mycielskian $\mu(G)$ adds shadow vertices $u_v$ for each $v$, connecting $u_v$ to $N_G(v)$, plus an apex. Starting from $K_2$, iteration gives $\chi(M_k) = k$ while remaining triangle-free.
mathContext: The Mycielskian $\mu(G)$ of a graph $G = (V, E)$ has vertex set $V \cup \{u_v : v \in V\} \cup \{w\}$, with edges $E \cup \{u_v x : vx \in E\} \cup \{wu_v : v \in V\}$. Mycielski proved $\chi(\mu(G)) = \chi(G) + 1$ and that $\mu(G)$ is triangle-free when $G$ is. This was the first proof that the chromatic number and clique number can be arbitrarily far apart, refuting the early conjecture that $\chi(G)$ depends only on $\omega(G)$.

title: Rödl's Theorem (1977)
content: **Axiom** (Rödl, 1977): For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists $f_k$ such that any graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \geq f_k$ contains a triangle-free spanning subgraph $H$ with $\chi(H) \geq k$. This is the core result solving Problem #923.
mathContext: Published in *Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.* **64** (1977), 370--371, Rödl's remarkably short proof works by edge-coloring $G$ based on triangle participation and applying Ramsey's theorem to extract a monochromatic triangle-free subgraph retaining high chromatic number. Each Ramsey application exponentiates the required chromatic number, leading to the tower-type bound $f_k \leq \text{tower}(O(k))$.

title: erdos_923_true
content: The corollary `erdos_923_true` directly restates Rödl's theorem as the affirmative answer to Problem #923. The proof is `:= rodl_1977`, a definitional equality since the type signatures are identical.
mathContext: This theorem serves as the human-readable formal answer: Problem #923 is TRUE. The proof is trivial (identity on the axiom) because the statement of `erdos_923_true` is literally the same as `rodl_1977`. The separation into axiom + corollary is a stylistic choice to distinguish the mathematical result from its problem-answer packaging.

title: Tower Function
content: **towerFunction**: $\text{tower}(0) = 1$, $\text{tower}(n+1) = 2^{\text{tower}(n)}$. Gives the sequence $1, 2, 4, 16, 65536, 2^{65536}, \ldots$ The first four values are verified by `rfl`, and $\text{tower}(4) = 65536$ by `native_decide`.
mathContext: The tower function $\text{tower}(n) = 2 \uparrow\uparrow n$ (Knuth up-arrow notation) grows faster than any fixed iteration of exponentiation. $\text{tower}(5) = 2^{65536}$ has approximately $19{,}728$ decimal digits. Tower-type bounds are characteristic of Ramsey theory: the Hales-Jewett numbers, Szemerédi regularity applications, and Shelah's bounds all involve tower-type growth.

title: Rödl Tower Bound
content: **Axiom**: $f(k) \leq \text{tower}(C \cdot k)$ for some universal constant $C$. Graphs with $\chi \geq \text{tower}(C \cdot k)$ must contain a triangle-free subgraph with $\chi \geq k$.
mathContext: The tower bound is believed to be qualitatively tight: the iterated Ramsey argument suggests $f(k)$ cannot be bounded by any function growing slower than tower-type. This parallels the situation in the Hales-Jewett theorem, where primitive recursive upper bounds were not known before Shelah's proof. The question of whether $f(k)$ is exactly tower-type or merely tower-bounded remains open.

title: H-Free Subgraph Problem
content: `HFreeSubgraphProblem H Hgraph`: for any fixed graph $H$, does $\chi(G) \geq f_H(k)$ imply $G$ has an $H$-free subgraph with $\chi \geq k$? This generalizes the triangle case ($H = K_3$) to arbitrary forbidden subgraphs, connecting to Erdős Problem #108.
mathContext: When $H$ is bipartite, the answer is YES (Rödl). When $H$ contains an odd cycle, the problem is more subtle. The general Erdős-Hajnal-type question for non-bipartite $H$ connects to Problem #108, which asks about subgraphs with large girth and high chromatic number. Note that the definition omits the $H$-freeness condition on the subgraph (only requiring high $\chi$), which is a simplification of the full problem.

title: Rödl's General Theorem for Bipartite H
content: **Axiom** (Rödl): The $H$-free subgraph problem holds whenever $H$ is bipartite (2-colorable). Bipartiteness is formalized as the existence of a `Coloring (Fin 2)` for $H$.
mathContext: The bipartite case is special because the Kővári-Sós-Turán theorem provides $\text{ex}(n, K_{r,s}) = O(n^{2-1/r})$, giving quantitative control on the density of $H$-free subgraphs. Rödl's general proof extends the triangle-free argument using bipartite Ramsey numbers. For non-bipartite $H$ (e.g., odd cycles $C_{2t+1}$), different techniques are needed, and the full generalization remains an active area connecting to Erdős Problem #108.
